top.line: Why event platforms block sites like PrompTugal.news, who owns a listing, what the law allows, and how we collect now.
top.para: A legal basis and evidence for every event.

in-short.line: Platforms forbid; organisers own; facts free; descriptions and photos not; guests never; our routes.

puzzle.line: Organisers want their events seen and a listing sends traffic back, yet the platforms block it.

terms.line: Eventbrite and Partiful forbid scraping; Luma only its interfaces and no images; Meetup's API is paid.

owner.line: The organiser owns the listing; platforms hold non-exclusive licences and distribute to partners they choose.
owner.para: So the organiser can license us.

law.line: Facts free; descriptions and photos the author's; database right and contracts limit wholesale copying.

expect.line: Organisers rarely complain; scrapers are sold openly; the honest route is to ask the organiser.

ourselves.line: A storm-day house rule stopped our agents even reading the platforms' terms.
ourselves.para: Part of the block was us.

collect.line: Official agendas, discovery for leads, facts and a link, organisers' submissions, a register, requests on record.

next.line: Read the terms, ask organisers, try organisers' interfaces, keep guests out, publish answers.

limits.line: Not legal advice; some terms from archives; no platform has answered yet.

sources.line: Platform terms, robots files, CJEU cases, statutes, the ICO and PrompTugal.news's events site.
